title: Tramon Mark, Matas Vokietaitis spark Texas to win over FDU in possiber harbinger of things to come - NewsBreak
text:
By Kirk Bohls ,
11 minutes ago Texas guard Tramon Mark led the Longhorns with a team-high 20 points in Wednesday's win over Fairleigh Dickinson in Austin. (Mikala Compton/Austin American-Statesman) AUSTIN — Sean Miller always looks ahead.
The first-year Texas basketball coach does so because in some important ways, he believes the NCAA selection committee looks, well, backward.
“College basketball is upside down in many ways,” he said. “When you look at March, March Madness is on everyone’s mind. And making the tournament is everyone’s goal. They show a team’s résumé, and most of the time they talk about November and December. Who did you play, where did you play and did you win?”
That panel may be the only ones who remember Texas’ convincing 93-58 win over Fairleigh Dickinson in front of an announced crowd of 9,820 at Moody Center because, after trailing 10-2 in the early going, the Longhorns caught their stride and ran away from the Northeast Conference school from New Jersey.
Tramon Mark and Matas Vokietaitis might reflect back on the team’s third game of the season, too, because they spurred the Longhorns to an easy win over 0-3 FDU to improve to 2-1 on the season.

They were the two central characters in Wednesday’s game and figure to be for the bulk of the season. Mark has shifted from point guard, where he started in the season-opening loss to Duke , to shooting guard, the position he played all year until last year’s SEC Tournament and brief NCAA Tournament run.
Wasn’t so much a run as it was a brisk walk, however, when a team played just one game and fell to Miller’s former Xavier team in a First Four contest in Dayton, Ohio.
This Texas shows much more pace, physicality and promise as a remade team that offers a healthy dose of newcomers to go with Mark, the 6-foot-5 guard who is one of four returners from Rodney Terry’s club that never got much traction.
Between Mark’s third 20-point game as a Longhorn over the past two seasons and the 19 points from the 7-foot Vokietaitis — two points off his career high — Texas scored on the former’s frequent drives to the basket and pair of treys and the center’s physical presence down low.
That should be a sweet recipe for success this season as Jordan Pope takes over the point guard spot and frees up Mark to find shots wherever he likes.
Texas had four players in double digits Wednesday and would have easily surpassed the century mark, had it not connected on just 19 of 34 free throws and a below-average six of 23 long-range shots.
“Tramon and Matas combined to be too much for FDU,” Miller said. “They were 17 for 21 from the field. That’s 39 points and high efficiency. Both guys were really terrific. They ended up being the difference, but we left a lot of points on the board. The free throws were part of the storyline, and we’ve got to convert at a better rate than that.”
